leverage.exposure: None. The total committed across all three live bids is comfortably below the cash balance, so even a clean sweep of every auction leaves the balance positive. No leveraged position exists and none can open from the bids as placed. Spending is capped well above anything in play here, so the floor is not binding either. The only real exposure is structural rather than financial: the transfer window shuts this evening and if Sylla is removed from the league before enough buys have landed, the squad loses a slot without warning.

binding_gap: One outfield body. Any outfield player at all fixes the shape from where he stands, and the first auction resolves within the hour, so the gap most likely closes on its own tonight. The safety net only matters if all three auctions are lost, and the board still holds several cheap outfield bodies with runways stretching past tomorrow, so there is no need to panic-buy.

verdict.headline: Do nothing tonight.
verdict.detail: Do nothing tonight. All three bids are placed at the right premiums and the first resolves within the hour — raising any of them now would only bid against himself. The one thing that changed this run is a correction to the standing plan, not a new trade: the previous instruction to sell Sylla the moment any buy lands was a trap. One buy landing leaves the squad exactly legal with zero slack, so a sale immediately after it would put him back below a fillable eleven and hand back the hundred-point penalty he is trying to escape. The rule is now: sell nothing until the squad is at twelve or more.

sell.reason: No sale is possible or wise right now. Selling requires having bought first, and even once that allowance exists a sale below twelve players re-opens the penalty. When the squad does reach twelve, Widmer is the first sale, not Sylla — he is the lowest scorer, is a confirmed non-starter, and raises so little that letting him go costs nothing in the fielded eleven. Bernardo follows him: he carries a fitness flag from the opening weekend and his value is bleeding faster than anyone else's. Sylla and Lokonga must never be sold as a pair; that combination leaves a shape with too many defenders and too few forwards to field at all.

Sell the moment the allowance exists.

In the 6 hours to 2026-09-01T00:40Z, David bought THREE players straight off the Kickbase board at or just BELOW mv, all with no fielding value: Pimpong (14920, Frankfurt ATT) 2.751.290 vs mv 2.760.937 = MINUS 0,35%; Guether (13629, Union Berlin MID) 2.941.280 vs mv 2.950.479 = MINUS 0,31%; Konoplia (7774, Gladbach DEF) 1.211.009 vs mv 1.219.089 = MINUS 0,66% - and get_player confirms Konoplia carries st=1, "Partial tear of medial collateral ligament in the knee - out for several weeks". Linguini07 paid 1.721.810 for Awortwie-Grant (8984, Paderborn DEF) against mv 1.545.176 = PLUS 11,43%, and get_player confirms st=1, "Lateral ligament injury - out for about 6 weeks". PhiL95 and Goran1992 ran the usual same-minute round trips (Quetant buy 1.637.900 / sell 1.650.813; Gendrey buy 2.558.595 / sell 2.564.595; Mohya buy 9.901.900 / sell 9.912.711) - margins of a few tenths of a percent on the daily tick. THIS IS MOTION, NOT POINTS. Georg optimises for points; buying a man who is out for six weeks to earn 0,3% on a market-value tick consumes a squad slot he cannot spare at 10 players and scores zero on MD2. The Awortwie-Grant clearing is however a genuine premium datapoint worth keeping: +11,43% over mv on a contested Kickbase listing for an injured player, which sits between the manager-ask low cluster and the Ebnoutalib/Campbell high cluster and further supports bidding the HIGH cluster on Kickbase board listings. NO REVERSAL - the flip mechanism is separately dead this run anyway: kb_context measures ZERO manager asks below mv.

movers.reason: No flip clears its cost this run. There are no manager asks below market value at all, so the mechanism a value trade depends on is simply absent. What the feed does show is worth naming so it is not mistaken for a signal: rivals spent the evening buying players off the board at or just under market value and reselling them minutes later for fractions of a percent, and in two cases the player bought is out for weeks with a knee or ligament injury. That is motion, not points, and it costs a squad slot he cannot spare.

Bernardo remains the single flag: Kickbase still marks him as knocked from the opening match, though he is absent from the injury table, so treat him as doubtful rather than ruled out. On the live bids, both large targets are confirmed fit and started the opening weekend; the cheap midfielder made his debut off the bench and is a body rather than a points source.
